source.section: TC-40 lines 4 to 22 (Instructions PDF p.9 Line 4; PDF p.10 Lines 5 to 20 and the Line 17 table; PDF p.11 Line 22); Line 21 and Qualified Exempt Taxpayer Worksheet lines 1 to 5 (PDF pp.10-11); (57) Municipal Bond Interest (PDF p.18); (71) Utah Municipal Bonds (PDF p.19)

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages (person 0) 24,000.00 = 24,000.00. Federal taxable income = 24,000.00 - standard deduction 23,625.00 = 375.00 (federal senior deduction ignored; Utah starts from federal AGI). TC-40 (head of household): line 4 federal AGI 24,000.00. Line 5 additions: code 57 municipal interest from other states 30,000.00, 30,000.00. Line 6 = 24,000.00 + 30,000.00 = 54,000.00. Line 7 state tax refund 0.00. The other-state bonds were bought after Jan. 1, 2003 from a state that taxes interest on Utah's bonds, so code 57 applies. Line 8 subtractions 0.00. Line 9 Utah taxable income = 54,000.00 - 0.00 - 0.00 = 54,000.00. Line 10 = 54,000.00 x 0.045 = 2,430.00. Lines 11 to 16, by the projection: no dependents; the deduction on line 12 is held as the cap 23,625.00; initial credit = 0.06 x min(line 9 54,000.00, cap 23,625.00) = 0.06 x 23,625.00 = 1,417.50. Line 17 base phase-out amount 27,320.00. Line 18 = max(0, 54,000.00 - 27,320.00) = 26,680.00. Line 19 = 26,680.00 x 0.013 = 346.840. Line 20 = max(0, 1,417.50 - 346.840) = 1,070.660. Line 21 worksheet: line 1 federal AGI 24,000.00; line 2 standard deduction 23,625.00; line 3 senior deduction 0.00 (no amount in Utah's sources); line 4 23,625.00; line 5 = max(0, 24,000.00 - 23,625.00) = 375.00. Line 5 is above zero, so not exempt; line 21 blank. Line 22 and TC-40A Part 3: line 20 1,070.660 = 1,070.660; credits 1,070.66. Tax = 2,430.00 - 1,070.66 = 1,359.34. Over the head of household threshold the exemption goes.
